record: CR-01C3D acceptance -- First real inventory-visible mod item
sanity_run_first: research/instrument-runs/2026-08-29T112301Z-c3c-sanity-armed (CR-01C3C re-run PASS with the hardened teardown)
what_this_proves: The framework created an item definition that did not exist in the game, published it through the registry the game actually reads, and the vanilla inventory code accepted it: a real S_InvItem carrying our FName appeared in the real player's Inventory array. It was then removed and every layer rolled back to an exact baseline.

0_teardown_invariant_hardened_first.rule: Shutdown requested -> stop handshake completes -> wait_stopped_ok == 1 -> ONLY THEN FreeLibrary. On any failure, timeout, exception or unconfirmed handshake the module is LEFT LOADED and the run reports BLOCKED-TEARDOWN.
0_teardown_invariant_hardened_first.also_covered: when the module is left loaded, the remote IO block is left allocated too -- the loaded module still holds g_io, and freeing it would leave a live dispatcher writing into unmapped memory, which is the same failure one indirection further out
0_teardown_invariant_hardened_first.implementation: research/instruments/ipp/probe_teardown.py, used by all three armed controllers; no controller calls FreeLibrary itself any more
0_teardown_invariant_hardened_first.enforced_by_tests: tests/test_probe_teardown.py -- 12 tests, including one that reproduces the exact failure shape that crashed the game (a raising read-back of the shared IO block) and asserts the module is NOT unloaded, plus source-level tests that no controller unloads on its own and that the handshake offsets agree with each controller's own full unpack

1_item_identity.interned_FName: 2245448 (the engine minted it via reflected KismetStringLibrary::Conv_StringToName)
1_item_identity.collision_check: the key was verified absent from all 496 MasterItemList rows and from the player inventory before anything was armed
1_item_identity.neutral_trigger_name: misery__c3d_neutral_trigger (FName 2245462), distinct from the row name and absent from ItemList

2_definition.everything_else: left exactly as UScriptStruct::InitializeStruct produced it. No FString/FText/TArray/soft-reference assignment mechanism was introduced to make the item prettier.
2_definition.decay_gate_checked_on_the_REAL_row: UseItemDecay (S_ItemDetails+1976) and UseDurability (+1928) were read off the materialized row: both 0. The run would have refused to reach AddItem if UseItemDecay were set, because DecayTime=0 would then have been an unproven choice.

3_S_InvItem_construction.derivation: not guessed -- every occupied slot of every live inventory component was decoded first: 1036 real vanilla entries across 1627 inventories
3_S_InvItem_construction.QuickBindIndex: -1 in 1036 of 1036 live entries. A zeroed struct would carry 0, which reads as 'bound to quick slot 0'. This is the field that would have been silently wrong.
3_S_InvItem_construction.Durability_and_DecayTime: inert for this definition because UseDurability and UseItemDecay are both 0; 100.0 and 0 were chosen to match the observed norm rather than to matter

4_publication_and_resolution.runtime_table: spawned via reflected UGameplayStatics::SpawnObject into /Engine/Transient, rooted through the CR-01A engine path in the same GameThread job, RowStruct set to the live S_ItemDetails pointer, populated with the CR-01C2R materializer while DETACHED
4_publication_and_resolution.attach: ParentTables element[1] = the Runtime table, Num 1 -> 2, into pre-existing spare capacity; Data and Max unchanged (no reallocation)
4_publication_and_resolution.publication: one data-neutral RemoveRow(ItemList, <a name it does not contain>); the engine rebuilt the composite through its own delegate path

resolver_check_before_AddItem.function: BP_SGKFunctions_C::'SGK ItemDetails' -- the function the inventory path itself uses, reading MasterItemList
resolver_check_before_AddItem.out_param_lifecycle: the 2272-byte S_ItemDetails out-param was constructed with InitializeStruct before the call and destroyed with DestroyStruct after, so the reflected call leaks nothing

5_addItem.call: exactly ONE BP_MasterInventory_C::AddItem on the live BP_PlayerInventory, on the proven GameThread dispatcher
5_addItem.out_params_were_NOT_treated_as_proof: the acceptance criterion is the inventory array itself; a successful ProcessEvent with no observable entry would have been NOT-PASS and would have triggered the rollback

6_inventory_observation_THE_KEY_RESULT.slot_relationship: RootIndex == SelfIndex == 0 and the slot's Inventory pointer is the player inventory, consistent with a 1x1 item occupying a single root slot; NewItemSlot.Index == 0 agrees with the observed slot index
6_inventory_observation_THE_KEY_RESULT.changed_slots: exactly one -- slot 0, in fields occupied (0->1), item.ID (0->probe), item.Amount (0->1), item.UseAmount (1->0). No other slot changed.

7_removal.path: BP_MasterInventory_C::RemoveItem(the observed S_InvSlot, RemoveWeight=1, RemoveInvAmount=1, SpecialSlot=0)
7_removal.why_this_path: established BEFORE any mutation as the exact inverse of AddItem: its Blueprint callees are RemoveItemWeight + ChangeItemCount + SetNewSlotItem, and its engine-maintained object-reference array holds only 5 entries with no spawn, drop or world path
7_removal.the_bools_were_inferences_so_they_were_n: instead of assuming the flags were right, the acceptance criteria require CurrentWeight and ItemCount to return to their exact baseline values -- an observation, not an assumption
7_removal.byte_identical_not_merely_semantic: the whole 12-slot array hashes identically to the baseline, so no normalization or mask was needed for the inventory comparison at all

8_registry_rollback.ordering: the inventory entry was removed FIRST; the definition was only unpublished once no S_InvItem carried its ID
8_registry_rollback.detach: Num 2 -> 1, same data-neutral trigger, composite rebuilt to 496 with the probe absent
8_registry_rollback.ParentTables_raw_baseline: {data 0x1ec5f15ced0, num 1, max 2, slots ['0x1ec66421000','0x0']} -- identical to baseline including the spare slot
8_registry_rollback.vanilla: all 496 names present and semantically unchanged after publication, after detach and at the end; ItemList byte-exact throughout and never written

9_health.game: pid 11548 still running and Responding after the run
9_health.verify_install: full mode, 0 serious and 0 benign findings, before AND after

10_residual_risks: Save/load and level-change survival of a published parent and of a runtime-created inventory entry -- BLOCKED ON M4 LIFECYCLE EVIDENCE.
The item has an empty Name/ShortName/Description FText, so any UI that displays it shows blank. A proven FText assignment path is still missing and is a separate gate.
Behaviour when ParentTables has no spare capacity (Max == Num): fails closed by design; no growth path is derived or authorised.
Multi-mod arbitration is designed but unexercised -- this run published one row from one table.
Whether native code caches raw composite row pointers across frames; a publication rebuild invalidates all of them.
The three RemoveItem bools are inferences validated only by the counters returning to baseline; a definition whose removal has additional side effects might not be covered by that check.
All multiplayer questions. This gate ran standalone with zero live NetDriver instances and refuses to run otherwise.
